To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
delayed flow-mediated vasodilator response associates with critical coronary artery stenosis.
the delayed or absence of brachial artery vasodilation associates with critical coronary artery disease and with a more severe degree of coronary stenosis.
delayed flow-mediated dilation of brachial artery associates with critical coronary artery stenosis and is a marker of the severity of coronary artery disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of atherosclerosis and its progression.
the study of atherosclerosis in a clinical setting, where the endothelial dysfunction and arterial wall thickness are associated with the severity of the disease.
the study of the association between delayed or absent dilation, critical coronary stenoses and the severity of coronary artery disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
endothelial dysfunction is an early manifestation of atherosclerosis and is a risk factor for coronary stenosis.
the kinetic of brachial artery response to ischemia is a marker of the severity of coronary artery disease.
the absence of a delayed response is more likely associated with severe coronary artery disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absence of dilation is an independent marker of severe atherosclerotic coronary artery disease.
delayed or absent flow-mediated dilation of brachial artery associates with critical coronary artery stenosis.
the kinetic of arterial dilation, rather than the magnitude, is more relevant for the severity of coronary disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endothelial function is a marker of coronary stenosis severity, as it is associated with the degree of coronary atheroma burden.
delayed flow-mediated dilation is associated with coronary stenotic lesions.
the kinetic of dilation is a relevant parameter in the evaluation of endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerosis.
